guards.what: G-new: Event.offer_card_reward skips Hook.ModifyRewards, and needs a reroll surface to fix
guards.maps_to: events/base.py::Event.offer_card_reward -- no apply_reward_modifiers, no reroll surface
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): THE REROLL SURFACE IS BUILT. Event.offer_card_reward -- a take-or-skip protocol with nowhere for a reroll flag to attach -- is DELETED (no callers left); the_future_of_potions now builds a real CombatRewards + populated CardRewardGroup on the pending_rewards channel, so the screen reaches driver._offer_card_group and gets C#'s single {cards..., Skip, REROLL} surface (CardRewardAlternative.cs:53-74, reached from CardReward.cs:189). VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, both directions: pre-fix (HEAD loaded into a throwaway process) the screen raised only EVENT + SELECT_CARDS and never REWARD_CARD, so the reroll was STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE; post-fix it raises REWARD_CARD, offers the reroll at slot n+1, redraws different cards from the same filtered pool, returns a card at upgrade_level 1, and is one-shot. Regeneration matches CardReward.cs:156-164/:322-332 (Reroll clears _cards and re-enters Populate's draw branch, re-firing AfterGenerated per TheFutureOfPotions.cs:129), and since RerollOptions == Options for the 3-arg ctor (:114-115) the pool-carrying subclass is the right shape. The reward modifiers dispatch EXACTLY ONCE end-to-end under round 13's consolidated choke point (state-mutating spy: 1 plain + 1 late, the offer-time backstop no-opping on CombatRewards.generated). WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: 'it needs new capability, not a missing call' -- correct as far as it went, but it bundled TWO different things. The selector half was settled separately in round 13 (and the 'take-or-skip screens auto-accept in real play' claim turned out to be WRONG for THIS screen: its decline already worked through RunState.select_cards's skippable-purpose machinery -- see this record's R6 note). The reroll half is what actually needed capability, and this is it. NOTE: building it exposed TWO further live divergences on the same screen, recorded as their own guard on this record -- the creation carried NEITHER IsCardReward NOR NoUpgradeRoll, so Silken Tress/Silver Crucible silently declined and the screen burned 3 extra Rewards draws while offering +2 cards where C# offers +1.  The text it replaced read: G-new (found 2026-07-31, tier-2 campaign, Task 32 -- OPEN, deliberately not fixed): Event.offer_card_reward (events/base.py) never dispatches the reward modifiers, so this event's card reward cannot be rerolled with Driftwood held, where C#'s RewardsSet.GenerateWithoutOffering (RewardsSet.cs:136) applies Hook.ModifyRewards to every RewardsSet. UNLIKE the two sibling sites fixed in the same task, this one is NOT a missing call: events/base.py's protocol is a boolean take-or-skip screen with no reroll surface at all, so closing it needs new capability, not a dispatch. Sole caller: the_future_of_potions.py. LIVE by the same argument as its siblings (the event and Driftwood are both ported). Confirmed real by the Task 32 reviewer. R6 update (2026-08-01, round 13): the wiring concern below is RESOLVED for the potion half and CORRECTED for the card half. Event._accept_offer (events/base.py) now falls back onto run.reward_selector -- the seam every RunDriver already wires unconditionally (driver.py:303) for RunState.offer_relic/offer_potion -- for purpose == 'potion' when no reward_offer_selector is explicitly installed, so drowning_beacon / endless_conveyor / potion_courier (x3) / the_legends_were_true / wellspring / whispering_hollow's potion offers are now real REWARD_POTION decisions in real play and in the conformance _ForceWinDriver, not permanent auto-accepts. For purpose == 'card_reward' (THIS event's own screen) the 'auto-accept in real play' characterization was WRONG once a driver is attached: offer_card_reward's downstream run.select_cards('card_reward', ...) was ALREADY skippable (driver.py's SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES, wired unconditionally via run.card_selector, driver.py:301) independently of reward_offer_selector -- proven against the PRE-R6 code by driving it with a real RunDriver (a decline-everything policy left the deck at 10 vs 11 for take) and pinned by test_the_future_of_potions_card_offer_already_declines_through_select_cards. _accept_offer deliberately leaves card_reward a pass-through rather than adding a second, redundant ask on top of the one that already worked. run.reward_offer_selector itself remains a TEST-ONLY override with zero production writers BY DESIGN (driver.py never assigns it; only test/test_event_offer_screens.py sets it) -- it is no longer load-bearing, because _accept_offer reaches the driver through run.reward_selector for potion offers instead. A repo-wide grep finding reward_offer_selector unwired by driver.py is EXPECTED, not a re-opened gap. THE REROLL-SURFACE GAP IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS OPEN, and it belongs on the REWARD_CARD decision, NOT on SELECT_CARDS: C# puts Skip and REROLL as alternatives on the card-selection screen itself (CardRewardAlternative.cs:53-74, reached from CardReward.cs:189), which the sim already models at driver.py:207-214 / _offer_card_group (driver.py:519-542). Closing it most likely means routing Event.offer_card_reward through run.offer_rewards (picking up apply_reward_modifiers via R10's offer-time backstop, run.py:530-561) and retiring _accept_offer's card_reward pass-through, not extending RunState.select_cards. WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: the claim that the wiring gap was 'pre-existing... needs its own task' UNDIFFERENTIATED across both purposes. It was not undifferentiated -- one purpose ('potion') had a real, fixable gap; the other ('card_reward') never had the gap the note implied, because a different, already-existing mechanism already covered it. NOTE: this entry stays a LIVE gap -- the reroll half is untouched.  The paragraph it replaced read: SEPARATE, LARGER CONCERN recorded here for want of a better home: run.reward_offer_selector is never wired by driver.py (set only in test files, verified by repo-wide grep), so take-or-skip screens AUTO-ACCEPT in real play. That is pre-existing and out of Task 32's scope, but it is a bigger divergence than the reroll flag and needs its own task.

guards.what: the flag set this screen's CardCreationOptions carry (IsCardReward + NoUpgradeRoll) -- both were absent
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13, R2 fix pass). CardCreationOptions.ForNonCombatWithUniformOdds ORs NoUpgradeRoll (CardCreationOptions.cs:159-162), TheFutureOfPotions.cs:127 ORs NoRarityModification | NoCardPoolModifications, and the CardReward constructor ORs IsCardReward onto Options AND RerollOptions unconditionally (CardReward.cs:114-115); WithFlags is `Flags |= flag` (CardCreationOptions.cs:212-216), so the creation runs against all four. THE SIM'S HAND-ROLLED create_reward_cards CALL CARRIED NONE OF THEM. Two consequences, both LIVE, both fixed: (a) IsCardReward absent -- Silken Tress (SilkenTress.cs:53-56) and Silver Crucible (SilverCrucible.cs:104-107) DECLINE when the flag is missing, so a player holding either got an un-enchanted / un-upgraded offer. Executed pre-fix (HEAD module, throwaway process): silver_crucible -> cards at +1, times_used=0; silken_tress -> no enchantment, is_used=False. Post-fix: +2 on every card (the late pass's +1 inside CardFactory.cs:104, then AfterGenerated's +1 at CardReward.cs:162) with times_used=1, and Glam attached. THIS IS THE SCREEN'S BUG, NOT THE RELICS' -- both relic ports are byte-faithful. (b) NoUpgradeRoll absent -- CardFactory.cs:98-102 guards the ENTIRE RollForUpgrade call on the flag, and the rng.NextFloat() lives INSIDE RollForUpgrade (CardFactory.cs:290), so C# takes 3 Rewards draws for this screen and never pre-upgrades. The sim took 6 and, in acts >= 1, could pre-upgrade a card that AfterGenerated then upgraded again -- offering +2 where C# offers +1. Executed pre-fix (act 2): draws=6, [('armaments',2),('havoc',2),('shrug_it_off',2)]; post-fix draws=3, all +1. CONFORMANCE-VISIBLE: the draw-count change re-phases the Rewards stream and the card identities shift. FOUND ONLY BECAUSE THE LANE RE-DERIVED THE FLAG SET FROM THE FACTORY rather than from the one visible .WithFlags call -- it is invisible at act 0. REASONING REPLACED: the record previously reasoned about this screen's creation ONLY through the pool guard, whose enumeration covers the four NoCardPoolModifications-gated pool-wideners and no other flag-gated hook. It had no entry for IsCardReward (a different hook, TryModifyCardRewardOptionsLate) or for NoUpgradeRoll (not a hook at all, a CardFactory branch), so both divergences were invisible to it.
